newsitem.title: FRANCE: Renault holds firm on plant closing.
newsitem.headline: Renault holds firm on plant closing.

text.p: France's new leaders are urging Renault to consider alternatives to closing a plant in Belgium, but the carmaker repeated Tuesday it had no choice.

"It seems what is needed, and it's what the factory's staff are seeking, is the opening of negotiations and discussions, which hasn't been done," said Elisabeth Guigou, who is widely expected to become the European Affairs minister in France's new Socialist government.
Her comments came as Renault met with its European workers to discuss the closure of the Vilvoorde plant, which sparked an outcry when it was announced in February.
Renault called the meeting after courts ruled it could not close the plant until it formaly consulted staff.
The company reiterated that the closure was essential not only to reduce costs, but also to streamline the company's money-losing car assembly operations in Europe.

It said it expected that after the new government looks carefully at the situation it will concede that tough measures are needed to save Renault, which lost 5.25 billion francs ($901 million) last year and is struggling to break even this year.
